title: Layered touchplay - midday scratchpad
content:
Midday sprint brain-dump - use this as the canonical temp list for calls + follow-ups today. NOT polished. Quick wins first, heavy-discovery later.

Today focus: re-engage 3 stalled trials (mid-market), demo invites, and 2 new inbound accounts that looked promising but didn’t reply. 4pm block is reserved for deep-custom notes + demo prep.

Priority list (call order):
1) NimbusHealth - contact: Sara Dunn (Head of ML Ops) - last touch 2026-07-16 (trial started but stalled on onboarding). Key note: wants private deployment for PHI redaction.
   - Quick hook: "We can spin a Private node for pilot with KMS integration and guide infra team through network policy."
   - Ask: book 30m this week, get list of sample PHI flows they need to protect.
   - Todo: send calendar invite w/ mock network diagram (template in Confluence).

2) AtlasRetail (inbound) - contact: Marc Li - interest: embeddings for search
   - Short script: "embedding-based search reduces search latency and increases conversion on top queries."
   - Objection prep: cost per embedding vs FAISS local; mention Redwood Optimize recommendations and batching to cut token cost.
   - Next step: schedule 20m demo + send pre-demo questionnaire (3 q's).

3) Harrow Fintech - contact: Priyash Mehta - legal wants audit logs + SOC2 details.
   - Bring SRE notes and compliance brief.
   - If they push on on-prem only, escalate to solutions-eng.

4) OptiGov - contact: Claire Rios - follow up on canary rollout questions from last call.
   - Keep message concise; include rollback policy bullets and routing by policy (latency/cost tiers).

Cold / quick touches (scripts):
- Opening 15s: "Hey <name>, quick note — Redwood Inference helps teams drop 40–60% token spend on average by combining batching, prefix caching, and runtime quantization. Thought it might matter for your usage profile."
- If they ask about models: "We host curated open models and also verify performance profiles — can show latency/cost matrix in demo."

Follow-up email snippets to use (short):
- After voicemail: "Hi <name>, left a quick voicemail — can we grab 15 min to see if Redwood could cut inference spend and stabilize latency for your LLM features? Calendly link."
- After demo: "Thanks for your time — attaching notes, recommended config, and next steps (pilot scope + success metric)."

Personal ops checklist (TODAY):
- [x] Prep NimbusHealth network diagram template
- [ ] Send AtlasRetail pre-demo questionnaire (3 Qs)
- [ ] Pull SOC2 summary + redact for Harrow
- [ ] Draft OptiGov rollback one-pager
- [ ] Block 4–5pm for demo prep and script run-through
- [ ] Update CRM with call outcomes and next steps (tickets: JIRA-5428 follow-up)

Notes from earlier calls (fragments):
- Nimbus: infra lead complained about previous vendor's opaque quantization results — emphasize transparent quant metrics + sample report.
- Harrow: procurement timeline is 6–8 weeks, procurement requires paper trail of infra changes.
- Atlas: VP of Product is the real decision maker, Marc is champion but needs VP buy-in.

Questions to resolve before EOD:
- Do we have a templated KMS integration checklist I can attach? (ask infra-channel)
- Who on solutions-eng can join a Wed 11am call for Harrow? Ping Samir.

Random quick reminders (notes-to-self):
- Use "reduce token spend" language sparingly — better to lead with reliability for finance teams.
- Bring a short latency-cost chart for every demo (one slide).
- Update the pre-demo questionnaire with one security question about data residency.

End of pad. Will clean and move items to CRM tonight. If pulled into AE stand, bring OptiGov rollback bullet.
